# Noise interoperability vectors

`noise-vectors.json` is generated by `TestRemoteNoise` in
`internal/remote/noise_test.go`, using github.com/flynn/noise v1.1.0.
It covers Noise_IKpsk2_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s and
Noise_KK_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s (Noise revision 34,
https://noiseprotocol.org/noise.html).

All byte strings are hexadecimal. Static and ephemeral fields without a Public
suffix are private keys. These fixed keys and PSKs are test fixtures only.
Handshake and transport arrays are in wire order; sender identifies the sending
role. Each transport direction has its own nonce starting at zero. The KK vector
with an empty prologue includes nonces 255 and 256 in both directions to exercise
the little-endian nonce carry. Hash is the final handshake hash (channel binding).

Regenerate deliberately from the repository root:

```sh
UPDATE_NOISE_VECTORS=1 go test -run '^TestRemoteNoise$' ./internal/remote
```

Ordinary Go tests compare the file byte for byte with freshly generated output.
The TypeScript tests independently produce every recorded ciphertext and decrypt
Go's bytes. They run in workerd with Web Crypto entropy, without Node crypto APIs.

The Go constructor exposes flynn/noise's raw handshake and split cipher states;
its two split ciphers are ordered by initiator/responder direction, not local
send/receive. The TypeScript split maps those directions to local send/receive.
Handshake payloads and learned peer statics must remain provisional until the
handshake completes. Applications must frame Go messages at no more than 65535
bytes: flynn/noise's transport cipher does not enforce that Noise wire limit.
The TypeScript layer enforces it on both handshake and transport messages.
